title: Tensor-action and open-counit identities for finite-level projection maps
statement:
Use the finite coefficient ring $A=A_{E,n}$, $n\geq1$, and field $k$ of [def-pur-conventions]. All schemes are separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Work in their ambient small pro-etale derived categories with pullback and tensor [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]; write $P_u=Lu^*$, $R_u=Ru_*$ and $\otimes=\otimes_A^L$, and use the canonical tensor associators and the pullback/tensor comparisons $\mu_{u;N_1,N_2}:P_u(N_1\otimes N_2)\xrightarrow{\sim}P_uN_1\otimes P_uN_2$.

1. *Proper maps.* Let $u:V\to W$ be proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] and let $\pi_{u;M,N}:R_uM\otimes N\to R_u(M\otimes P_uN)$ be precisely the counit-defined projection map [def-exchange-projection]. For arbitrary $M\in D(V_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ and $N_1,N_2\in D(W_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$, under the associators and $\mu_u$,
$$\pi_{u;M,N_1\otimes N_2}=\pi_{u;M\otimes P_uN_1,N_2}\circ(\pi_{u;M,N_1}\otimes1_{N_2}).$$
2. *Open immersions.* Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion], with exact extension by zero $j_!\dashv j^{-1}$, counit $\varepsilon_j:j_!j^{-1}\to1$, and canonical tensor isomorphism $\delta_{j;M,N}:j_!M\otimes N\xrightarrow{\sim}j_!(M\otimes j^{-1}N)$ of [lem-cbc-extension-zero-projection-formula]. For arbitrary $M$ on $U$ and $N_1,N_2$ on $X$, under the associators and $\mu_j$,
$$\delta_{j;M,N_1\otimes N_2}=\delta_{j;M\otimes j^{-1}N_1,N_2}\circ(\delta_{j;M,N_1}\otimes1_{N_2}).$$
For arbitrary $F,N$ on $X$, as maps $j_!j^{-1}F\otimes N\to F\otimes N$,
$$\varepsilon_{j,F\otimes N}\circ j_!(\mu_{j;F,N}^{-1})\circ\delta_{j;j^{-1}F,N}=\varepsilon_{j,F}\otimes1_N.$$
3. *Compactifications.* For a separated finite-type morphism $f:X\to Y$ with a chosen compactification $c=(j,p)$, the compactification projection map $\operatorname{PF}^c_{f;M,N}:Rp_*j_!M\otimes N\to Rp_*j_!(M\otimes Lf^*N)$ of [def-exchange-projection] satisfies the tensor-action identity of clause 1, with $Rp_*j_!$ in place of $R_u$ and $Lf^*$ in place of $P_u$.

These are identities of the actual maps, before imposing invertibility on any projection map. The same assertions hold on the ordinary etale derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], using exact inverse image, ordinary derived tensor [def-kun-derived-tensor], the same counit-defined proper projection maps and open tensor isomorphisms, and the compactified compact-support functors $Rp_*j_!$ of [def-amb-etale-compact-support, lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons].

proof.text: Use the adopted source library's general left-derived tensor comparison. Its K-flat left derivability structure provides resolutions of every derived object, so ofLaxSquareHδ supplies its oplax associativity. Invert the tensor comparisons and cancel their composites to obtain inverse associativity; no derived unit comparison or full monoidal structure is needed. The canonical pro-etale comparison is definitionally this general comparison. This replaces the ringed-topos comparison route without changing any specified tensor map.

For proper maps apply Adjunction.rightAdjointProjectionMap_associativity to the canonical pullback comparison, on each site. Postcompose with the image of the inverse tensor associator and use functoriality and the isomorphism identities. This gives the requested action equation for the actual rightDerivedLowerStarProjectionMap, with no inverse projection map.

For an open immersion express the mixed tensor comparison using leftDerivedUpperStarIsoMapDerivedCategory and the inverse tensorator. Transport inverse tensor associativity across this natural isomorphism. Prove the projection-associativity calculation by the adjunction Hom equivalence, with the tensorator given explicitly, and invert the resulting equality of isomorphisms. On the ordinary etale site the adopted source already proves this inverse associativity. For the open-counit law prove the general projection/counit identity by injectivity of the adjunction Hom equivalence, naturality of the tensor comparison and the triangle identities; then cancel the open projection isomorphism.

The general leftDerivedTensorComparison_naturality_app and map_leftDerivedTensorComparison_app_app_comp show that the canonical pro-etale pullback-composition isomorphism respects the tensor comparison. Its underived comparison is monoidal by conjugating lowerStarComp. Normalize the compactification equality transport to leftDerivedUpperStarCongr before taking the inverse composition. Expand the compactification projection into the proper projection, the image of the inverse open projection and the pullback-composition comparison, using projectionMapOfCompactification_app_app. Prove the composite action calculation for these component families: proper naturality moves the two open factors across the second proper projection; proper and open action associativity combine each pair; the tensor coherence of the pullback-composition comparison identifies the resulting last map with the pullback of f. The remaining reassociation is monoidal coherence. This component calculation is proved with arbitrary categories before specialization, without comparing the entire natural-transformation structures of the derived bifunctors. On the ordinary etale site use its own proved inverse-open and tensor-composition coherences in the same calculation. The final interface retains all three canonical tensor bifunctors and their associators explicitly; a proved abstract transport along the defining tensor-functor and associator equalities avoids expanding the derived monoidal constructions during specialization. The specialization uses proved defining equalities for the three tensor bifunctors, heterogeneous equalities for their associators and pullback comparisons, and an explicit nested-object interface for the components of the composition isomorphism. Identify the canonical compactification projection with the composite component family by its source component formula, then rewrite its three occurrences in the action equation. Keep the composite functor objects in this final interface; expanding them into nested objects while comparing concrete derived-category types would force the kernel to unfold the localization construction.

Specialize these coefficient-category identities to ModuleCat of the positive-level coefficient ring in PurityFiniteSetting. Keep the original scheme, morphism and compactification hypotheses and the exact eight public statements unchanged. The argument is at the chosen compactification and does not use projection invertibility.
